# Education station: regulated deployment guide

<!-- Generated by scripts/gen-industry-guides.mts. Do not edit by hand. Regenerate: npm run gen-industry-guides. Drift check: npm run check:industry-guides -->

**Status:** experimental. AI-drafted; not reviewed by a qualified expert; not legal advice.

**Claim:** Self-reported · **Result:** not evaluated (no applicability decision is recorded) · **Evidence:** incomplete · **Enforcement:** none · **Review:** pending · **Applicability:** unresolved

This guide maps what AMC source provides for an agent deployed in the `education` station: its sector packs, the frameworks those packs name, the assurance packs, the deployment controls and the evidence AMC can produce. It is generated from source; every count is derived from source, and every source location is listed in the verification appendix and checked by `tests/industryGuides.test.ts`.

It does not say what any regulation requires, and it is not legal advice. Framework names below are strings that appear in AMC source; their presence means a pack refers to them, not that AMC satisfies them.

## Sector packs

Packs whose `stationId` is `education`, as returned by `getIndustryPacksByStation` [C7]. Every pack is labelled `contentStatus: "experimental"` [C8]: its questions and citations are AI-drafted and no qualified expert has reviewed them.

| Pack | Name | Questions | Risk tier | Self-assessment target |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `k12-pm3` | K-12 Education | 19 | critical | 80 |
| `higher-education` | Higher Education | 19 | very-high | 70 |
| `skills-training` | Skills & Vocational Training | 15 | high | 65 |
| `specialized-education` | Specialized Education | 18 | high | 65 |
| `differently-abled` | Differently Abled Education | 16 | very-high | 75 |

Total: 5 packs, 87 questions.

Run one with `amc domain pack run --pack <id>` [C9]. The command requires the industry-pack entitlement [C10]. In a terminal the operator picks a level per question (L1, L3 or L5) [C11]; with `--baseline`, or without a terminal, no question is answered, so every question is not evaluated and no score is computed [C12]. The answers are self-reported and cap the eligible level at L1 [C13], so a pack result is a self-assessment, not an observation of the agent. Meeting the self-assessment target certifies nothing.

## Frameworks referenced

- Station `regulatoryBasis` [C14]: `FERPA`, `COPPA`, `EU AI Act`, `GDPR`.
- Station `complianceFrameworks` [C15]: `FERPA`, `COPPA`, `EU AI Act`, `GDPR`.
- The station's packs name 40 distinct framework strings in their `regulatoryBasis` and `complianceFrameworks` fields [C16]: `FERPA 20 USC §1232g`, `COPPA 15 USC §6501-6506`, `CIPA`, `ESSA`, `IDEA`, `Section 508`, `UN CRC Article 28/29`, `GDPR (Children)`, `EU AI Act Annex III §3`, `COPPA 15 USC §6501`, `FERPA`, `AACSB/Regional Accreditation Standards`, `EU AI Act`, `UNESCO Higher Education Guidelines`, `GDPR`, `Title IX`, `ADA`, `Bologna Process`, `AACSB Standards`, `Bologna Process QF-EHEA`, `ILO VET Standards`, `UNESCO TVET Framework`, `EQF (European Qualifications Framework)`, `NQF Standards`, `ISO 21001`, `EQF`, `UNESCO Arts Education Guidelines`, `WHO ICF Framework`, `Section 508/WCAG 2.1`, `Creative Commons Licensing`, `ISTE Standards`, `Creative Commons`, `WCAG 2.1`, `CRPD (UN Convention on Rights of Persons with Disabilities)`, `WCAG 2.1 AA`, `EU Web Accessibility Directive`, `UDL Principles`, `UNESCO Salamanca Statement`, `CRPD`, `UDL Guidelines 2.2`.

`amc compliance report --framework <id>` accepts the ids of `ComplianceFramework` [C17], resolved by `normalizeFrameworkName` [C18]; an unresolved name is rejected [C19]. Of the 41 framework strings above (station and packs together):

- 4 resolve as written: `EU AI Act` → `EU_AI_ACT`, `GDPR` → `GDPR`, `GDPR (Children)` → `GDPR`, `EU AI Act Annex III §3` → `EU_AI_ACT`.
- None resolves only after replacing spaces and hyphens with `_`.
- 37 do not resolve to any `ComplianceFramework` id, so AMC has no built-in compliance map under those names.

Dated entries are in [the regulatory calendar](../REGULATORY_CALENDAR.md), generated from `GLOBAL_FRAMEWORKS` [C20] and the key dates of the sourced register [C21].

## Assurance packs

### Linked by the station registry

The station's `assurancePacks` field [C22] lists these packs. "Empty-response passes" counts scenarios whose validator passes an empty string; a nonzero count means the pack can pass without the agent producing anything.

| Pack | Title | Scenarios | Empty-response passes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `educationFERPA` | Education FERPA/COPPA Pack | 10 | 0 |

### Registered but not linked

Registered packs [C23] whose title contains one of the station's registry framework strings verbatim, but which the registry does not link. This is a name match, not a recommendation.

| Pack | Title | Scenarios | Empty-response passes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `technologyGDPRSOC` | Technology GDPR/SOC2/ISO27001 Pack | 5 | 0 |
| `euAiActArticle` | EU AI Act Article-Level Assurance Pack | 6 | 0 |

### How each command grades

- `amc domain assurance --agent <id> --domain education` [C24] runs the linked packs [C25] without invoking any agent, so every pack is reported not evaluated [C26]. With `--example` it grades a built-in synthetic reply [C27]; that output is a labelled synthetic example and never evidence about the agent.
- `amc assurance run --agent <id> --pack <packId>` sends each scenario prompt to the agent through its responder and grades the answer; see Evidence outputs below.

## Deployment controls

Nothing in source makes these controls station-specific: the native agent toolset registers the same guards for every agent, whatever its station [C28]. A guard can only deny, and the first guard that denies is the one reported [C29].

| Control | What the source does | Where |
|---|---|---|
| Prompt-injection guard | Refuses a tool call whose arguments match an injection pattern at block confidence. | [C30] [C31] |
| Runtime firewall | Evaluates each tool call's arguments. A workspace with no signed firewall policy blocks every call (mode `missing-policy`). | [C32] [C33] [C34] [C35] |
| Budgets | Native tool calls in EXECUTE mode reserve against the signed per-agent budget; with no signed budget for the agent the call is refused, and an exhausted daily tool budget refuses the action class. | [C36] [C37] [C38] [C39] [C40] |
| Budget status (advisory path) | `evaluateBudgetStatus` reports not-ok when the budgets file signature is invalid. It reports ok when the agent has no per-agent budget; the native admission path above does not. | [C41] [C42] [C43] |
| Network egress | A network tool call must name a URL whose host is on that tool's signed allowlist; an unlisted network tool is refused. | [C44] [C45] [C46] |
| Tool allowlist | Tools absent from the signed `tools.yaml` are denied when the config is deny-by-default; an unverifiable config denies every call. | [C47] [C48] [C49] [C50] |
| Sandbox | Native sandbox admission returns a permit only for the `bash` tool at action class WRITE_HIGH, on Linux (bubblewrap) or on macOS (seatbelt) unless the signed kind is the Linux-only `linux-bwrap`; the Docker sandbox runs with `--network none` unless a network or gateway route is named. | [C51] [C52] [C53] [C54] [C55] [C56] |
| Lease | Bridge requests carry a signed lease, checked for signature, expiry, revocation, agent, workspace, scope (default `gateway:llm`), route and model. | [C57] [C58] [C59] [C60] [C61] [C62] [C63] [C64] [C65] |

None of these controls was executed to write this guide. The table records where each is implemented; the tests that exercise them live with their source.

## Evidence outputs

| Output | How it is produced | Where |
|---|---|---|
| Signed receipts | Receipts are minted for LLM requests and responses, tool actions and results, guard checks and accepted wire work, and verified against public keys. | [C66] [C67] [C68] |
| Tool-call evidence rows | The native toolset records each tool call's evidence row through the session recorder, or appends it to the workspace ledger for a caller without one. | [C69] [C70] |
| Assurance report | `amc assurance run --agent <id> --pack <packId>` runs a pack against the agent through its responder. | [C71] [C72] [C73] [C74] |
| Domain report | The domain report builder writes Markdown when given an output path. | [C75] [C76] |
| Compliance report | `amc compliance report --framework <id>` (alias `comply`) writes a Markdown or JSON report; the Markdown appendix states it is not legal advice. | [C77] [C78] [C79] |
| Audit binder | `amc audit binder create` produces a signed `.amcaudit` artifact. | [C80] [C81] [C82] |
| Enterprise audit export | Audit records export as Splunk, Datadog, CloudTrail, Azure, Elasticsearch or syslog payloads. `buildSignedAuditTrail`, despite its name, attaches an integrity hash and a chain hash over the records and no signature. | [C83] [C84] [C85] |

No output above was produced for this guide. Each row names the function that produces it.

## Known gaps at this commit

- The registry's `questionCount` for this station is 6; the station has 5 packs and 87 questions, so the field equals neither the pack count nor the question total. Use the counts in Sector packs.
- 37 of 41 framework strings do not resolve to a compliance-report framework (see Frameworks referenced).
- The packs' 39 `regulatoryBasis` entries resolve to catalogue records with a status and review date where the catalogue has one [C86]; 0 resolve to no record and 21 to a record marked unverified, so those cannot show whether they are current.
- `amc domain assurance` invokes no agent, so its result is always not evaluated (see Assurance packs).
- Pack results from `amc domain pack run` are self-assessments capped at L1 (see Sector packs).
- Pack questions, deep questions and this guide are AI-drafted and experimental: no qualified expert has reviewed them.

## Education overlay draft

This draft is experimental, not reviewed, not legal advice. Promotion is `none`. The actual P1-13 domain is `education.schools-skills`. The preserved int046 inventory contains 87 pack and 16 handwritten deep questions, 103 unique IDs confirmed by root's historical clean-source Node v22.23.3 runtime inventory. The eight inventory source files remain unchanged after int52ad3 integration. Its hashed evidence reference is in `docs/catalog/education/dispositions.json`; the documentation subagent did not execute that command. `docs/catalog/education/dispositions.json` retains every actual question and the spec's count/label drift.

The four proposed signatures are exact teacher approval before a final-grade write (`L1-EDU-01`), an EU emotion-inference capability gate (`L1-EDU-02`, Art. 5(1)(f)), a P2-27 export-boundary wrapper (`L1-EDU-03`) and automated WCAG 2.1 A/AA checks on generated HTML (`L1-EDU-04`). Historical fixture evidence remains pinned to its original execution source in the preserved receipt. The integrated candidate requires its own source-bound verification and new receipt; no current execution total or pass is inferred here. Local synthetic observations never establish a school's result. Missing production evidence or enforcement leaves `not_evaluated` with enforcement `none`.

P2-27's two-institution FERPA fixture remains unavailable; its wrapper stays `not_evaluated` without a parallel authorization implementation. P2-30's experimental COPPA/marking drafts, P3-14's experimental FRIA draft and the optional guide hook are now available. Availability does not establish Education-specific applicability, admitted reuse evidence or production enforcement. This fragment uses the existing hook and adds no generator implementation. The existing composition is `education-technology`; both fixture profiles now declare the Education and Technology domains. The current compiler checks inspect their scope-specific Technology requirements, while empty production evidence remains `not_evaluated`/`none`. No Governance facts are invented to select FRIA; the existing Governance CUI candidate is not applicable. Neither composed catalog selection nor a synthetic observation establishes complete legal coverage. Learner age and institution-specific legal/approval facts remain unknown manual prerequisites.

Automated WCAG 2.1 checks cover only their automatable subset. They do not establish WCAG 2.2 authentication, assistive-technology interoperability, full Section 508 scope, an accessibility statement/feedback workflow or conformance across apps and media. The manual WCAG assessment remains OPEN with an unassigned specialist, criterion-level results and remediation required. No manual criterion passes by default.

All instrument metadata remains unverified and flagged for re-verification. No fresh regulatory text, legal review or new source retrieval is claimed. The privacy counsel and accessibility expert placeholders under D-14/D-10, P1-29 education partner, independent sign-offs, manual assessor and funded stewardship remain open. Support stays experimental until all ten admission criteria and Sid's promotion decision are satisfied.

An A4 catalog-lock change is `scope_changed`, never a fault; capture any applicable FRIA before P3-23 completion. This draft changes no A4 behavior.
